survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This OECD country note synthesises system-level indicators for Austria (e.g., education spending, attainment, unemployment, literacy from the Survey of Adult Skills/PIAAC, and teacher workforce statistics). It does not provide an analysis section with an explicit student-level sampling frame, replicate design, or weight variables (e.g., W_FSTUWT, BRR) that would allow replication of a microdata estimation. The figures are presented as descriptive statistics and cross-indicator comparisons using OECD indicator methodology rather than a single unified student-level model. Therefore, no specific complex-survey weight variable can be identified from the note; users should consult the referenced Education at a Glance 2025 Sources, Methodologies and Technical Notes for indicator-specific sampling and weighting details.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This document is a descriptive country note that reports indicator results (e.g., attainment shares, unemployment rates, literacy proficiency levels) rather than training or estimating a student-level predictive model with documented plausible values (PVs). PV handling is therefore not applicable because the note does not specify any PV-based achievement modeling pipeline (e.g., Rubin’s rules, WLE/theta, or PV averaging) for a defined dependent variable. Missing-data handling is not reported because the note does not describe any microdata processing or imputation/deletion strategy; instead it points readers to the OECD indicator technical notes for the underlying indicator construction.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used OECD Education at a Glance 2025 indicator data for Austria for the latest available reference year(s) across multiple underlying sources (e.g., Survey of Adult Skills/PIAAC for literacy and unemployment/attainment-related indicators, and administrative/education system statistics for teacher vacancies and instruction time). The note does not specify an analytic subsample definition (e.g., grade band, task/module completion, or exclusion rules) because it is not presenting a single microdata-based analytic sample.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD Education at a Glance 2025 country note for Austria summarises key education-system characteristics using the latest available indicator data across multiple domains (tertiary education emphasis, education spending, labour-market outcomes, adult literacy, and teacher workforce indicators). It reports descriptive comparisons such as education expenditure per student (USD (PPP) 20 942; third highest in the OECD), the association between parental education and tertiary attainment (63% vs 16% for young adults 25–34), and adult literacy proficiency shares from the Survey of Adult Skills/PIAAC (31% at or below Level 1). It also provides labour-market differentials by educational attainment (e.g., unemployment 18.3% without upper secondary vs 4.7% with tertiary) and teacher shortages/attrition trends (vacancies 4.6% and attrition rising to 6.2% by 2022/23). Because the note does not estimate a student-level predictive model, it does not report ML performance metrics, PV handling, or missing-data procedures; readers should consult the OECD technical notes for indicator-specific methodology.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This extraction corresponds to a descriptive OECD country note rather than an empirical large-scale assessment analysis with a defined student-level dataset, analytic sample, and ML modeling workflow. As a result, fields required for predictive ML studies (e.g., total_students, PV handling details for a modeled outcome, missing-data strategy, and main_findings as ML target predictions) are not applicable or not reported in the provided text. The note instead aggregates indicator results and directs readers to the Education at a Glance 2025 Sources, Methodologies and Technical Notes for the underlying data collection and indicator construction.
